story.title: Hammering on the Plank Road
story.text: Out in the open, the soldiers hammered at the plank road, so slowly that people laughed.
story.narration: In the first year of Han, Liu Bang and his army were shut out south of the Qin mountains. He sent men to rebuild the plank road in plain sight — board by board, so slowly that the guards on the other side laughed.

story.title: The Path at Night
story.text: By night, another group had already walked the back path into Chencang.
story.narration: By night, another group did not take the plank road at all. They climbed the mountain by a narrow path and slipped quietly into Chencang. By the time the other side noticed, they were already inside the city.

keyMoment.question: The plank road is going up very slowly. What do we do?

options.text: Keep building it for everyone to see, and go another way at the same time
Work extra hours and finish the plank road
options.hint: However fast you build, the other side keeps watching that road.
If the open work suddenly stops, they see at once that you are changing roads.

keyMoment.reveal: Hold up the open one, and the quiet one gets through — two things can be done at once.

misconceptions: If you are blocked, you can only stop and wait
Doing two things at once means doing both badly

quiz.question: Which road did the main army really take?
options: The narrow back path over the mountain to Chencang
quiz.explanation: The plank road was built for the other side to watch. The real army took the back path.

quiz.question: You want to finish your homework and practise the piano. How do you arrange it?
options: Do one of them out in the open and push the other along in the free moments
Only practise the piano and skip the homework
quiz.explanation: Hold up the one everyone can see, and push the other along in the free moments. Both get done.
